rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **discriminant** D = b² − 4ac is the complete root classifier: **D > 0** two distinct real roots (rational when D is a perfect square — NEB 2024's x² − 5x + 6 = 0 has D = 1, roots 2 and 3), **D = 0** a repeated root at −b/2a (tangency — k² − 36 = 0 gives k = ±6), **D < 0** conjugate complex roots.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - x = (−b ± √D)/2a; D = b² − 4ac - α + β = −b/a; αβ = c/a; α² + β² = (α+β)² − 2αβ; |α − β| = √D/|a| - reconstruction: x² − (α+β)x + αβ = 0

rows.text: "D > 0: two real roots; D = 0: repeated; D < 0: complex conjugates. alpha + beta = -b/a; alpha beta = c/a."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Tangency as D = 0*** - a repeated root means the parabola just touches the x-axis: the discriminant's zero case is a geometry statement.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Quadratics Fully Decoded The discriminant b² − 4ac governs everything: **nature of roots**, and the **Viète relations** sum = −b/a, product = c/a — the pair that converts root information into coefficient equations and back.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The quadratic formula and discriminant - **x = (−b ± √D)/2a**, D = b² − 4ac. - **Nature theorem:** D > 0 ⟹ two distinct real roots; **D = 0** ⟹ one repeated real root (−b/2a); **D < 0** ⟹ two conjugate complex roots (−b ± i√|D|)/2a. - **Perfect-square sub-case:** D > 0 and a perfect square ⟹ rational roots (factorable over ℚ).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Nature of roots: compute D first. Symmetric root expressions: Viete, never solve. Equal roots: set D = 0. New roots: new sum, new product, rebuild x^2 - Sx + P.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. (2m)** — **Factoring:** two numbers with product 6 and sum −5 are −2 and −3: x² − 5x + 6 = (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 ⟹ **x = 2 or x = 3**. **Viète verification:** the roots' sum is 2 + 3 = 5, matching −b/a = −(−5)/1 = 5 ✓; their product is 6, matching c/a = 6/1 ✓ — the root–coefficient relations…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0, find α² + β² and 1/α + 1/β without solving the equation.** — **Viète relations:** α + β = −b/a = 5/2 and αβ = c/a = 3/2. **Sum of squares:** α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ = (5/2)² − 2(3/2) = 25/4 − 3 = **13/4**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For "find k" questions, state the condition (D = 0, or a Viete relation) as a separate line - the condition is the theorem being tested.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Viete is a translation device: symmetric expressions in the roots convert to coefficients without ever solving the equation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Quadratic formula x = (-b +- sqrt(D))/2a with D = b^2 - 4ac. Nature theorem: D > 0 two distinct real roots (rational if D is a perfect square); D = 0 repeated root -b/2a (tangency); D < 0 conjugate complex roots.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Projectile range maximisation hides a D = 0 condition: the peak of a parabola is its repeated-root geometry in physics clothing.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): For what values of k does the equation x² + kx + 9 = 0 have (i) equal roots, (ii) real roots?** — **(i) Equal roots ⟺ D = 0:** D = k² − 4(1)(9) = k² − 36 = 0 ⟹ **k = ±6**.…

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Discriminant** | D = b² − 4ac — root classifier | D = 0: double root | | **Viète relations** | α+β = −b/a, αβ = c/a | sum/product from coefficients | | **Conjugate roots** | D < 0 gives z and z̄ | 1 ± i√3 | | **Repeated root** | D = 0: both roots −b/2a | (x−3)² = 0 |  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why the discriminant decides - √D must be real (D ≥ 0) or imaginary (D < 0); the formula's structure makes D the complete classifier — one number, three regimes. ### 4.2 Viète as a translation device - Many questions never ask for the roots — only for symmetric combinations (sums of squares, reciprocals).…  ·  ## 5. Comparison Tables **Discriminant regimes** | D | Roots | Graph | |---|---|---| | > 0 | two distinct real | cuts x-axis twice | | = 0 | repeated real | tangent to x-axis | | < 0 | conjugate complex | misses x-axis |

Common Confusions **Sum carries the minus:** α + β = −b/a — dropping the sign is the most common Viète error.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Complex roots come in conjugate pairs** only when coefficients are real — state the hypothesis.  ·  **|α − β| = √D/|a|:** the |a| in the denominator is forgotten when a is negative.  ·  ## 7. Exam Application **NEB 2024 (verified PYQ): Solve x² − 5x + 6 = 0. (2m)** — Factor: (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 ⟹ **x = 2, 3**. Viète check: sum 5 = −(−5)/1 ✓, product 6 = 6/1 ✓ — the root–coefficient relations confirm the factorisation.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): If α and β are the roots of 2x² − 5x + 3 = 0, find α² + β² and 1/α + 1/β.** — Viète: α+β = 5/2, αβ = 3/2. **α² + β²** = (α+β)² − 2αβ = 25/4 − 3 = **13/4**. **1/α + 1/β** = (α+β)/αβ = (5/2)/(3/2) = **5/3**. No root was ever computed — Viète did all the work.  ·  **NEB-style (3m): For what value of k does x² + kx + 9 = 0 have equal roots?** — Equal roots ⟺ **D = 0**: k² − 36 = 0 ⟹ **k = ±6**. For k = 6 the double root is −3; for k = −6 it is +3 — the sign of k only moves the root's position, not the tangency.  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Form the quadratic equation whose roots are 2 + √3 and 2 − √3.** — Sum = 4; product = 4 − 3 = 1. **Equation: x² − 4x + 1 = 0.** (The roots are conjugate surds, so the coefficients are rational — as guaranteed for quadratics with rational coefficients.)
